label: a year of the 1880s or 1890s written in digits (peaks on the decade digit: 18|8|x, 18|9|x, and '1890s'); years 1900-1909 fire about half as strongly; years of the 1870s fire weakly (about 0.12-0.26, on the 7); years before 1870 (including the 1850s-1860s, this neuron's other pole), the 1910s-1990s, 2000-2079 and earlier centuries stay quiet (under about 0.1); future years 2080-2099 used as years (and 'the 2090s') fire weakly (about 0.2-0.35); 1880s-1890s years spelled out in words fire weakly (about 0.1-0.3); a non-year 188x/189x number (a count, a distance, a price) is weak on its own (about 0.03-0.25), fires strongly (up to about 0.8) when a year of the 1880s or 1890s appears earlier in the text, is unreliable after an earlier 1850s-1870s year (sometimes strong, sometimes quiet), and stays weak after an earlier 20th-century year
